English.Text: Re-schooling
The Moot worry the Scholars have forgotten who they are and what they owe to their homeland— I can give them a good talking-to.
... Anniversary?! I said, but I'm this close to the first life-size replica of a Cleopatra Ferruginea shell!
...oh, it was a Wilde night all right - pun intended, of course!
... and where would you be without the fortunes my father pays this venerable institution, Hm?
'Momentously important work', tch, If the Lord wanted slugs to be important he'd have made us slugs!
How could he forget everything we taught him so easily! By the end he was squirming with shame!
Of all the arrogant, thankless young grasshoppers... Using someone else's hard work to settle his own petty argument.
Self-Important Researcher of Snails
Decadent Party-Goer
Daddy's Brat
The Elder fears the scholars (Mihurani) sent abroad are losing their grip on reality. She wishes you to bring one of the main culprits home so she can school him adequately.
The Elder wants to knock some sense and humility into the Scholars living abroad.
The Scholars are arguing in front of a crowd near the coast in the Old World
Choose a Scholar and bring him back to Enbesa
This scholar puts his 'important' work before everything else.
The scholar flaunts their love of uninhibited literary parties.
The Scholar loudly claims his father's donations grant him more freedoms than others.
The Elder relishes the guilt she made the Scholar feel.
The Elder is furious at the Scholar's arrogance.
Elder: You have met all three of those spoiled Scholar Mihurani. Which one deserves the most to be humbled and punished?
